title: Shah Rukh Khan's 'King' Locks Christmas 2026 — and Suhana Khan Is Walking Into a ₹350-Crore War Zone
excerpt: SRK returns as a lethal assassin opposite Abhishek Bachchan's villain, Suhana makes her theatrical debut, Deepika Padukone may cameo, and Anirudh scores the whole thing. Siddharth Anand's action thriller just became the most dangerous ticket in town.
body:
There's a reason Christmas in Bollywood belongs to Shah Rukh Khan. The man doesn't just release films during the holidays — he *becomes* the holiday. And now, after months of whispers, cryptic Instagram posts from director Siddharth Anand, and enough industry leaks to fill a season of *Koffee With Karan*, we finally have confirmation: King will arrive in cinemas on December 25, 2026.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Uu2QK9Z9X5E

The timing is surgical. By locking Christmas Day, the makers have carved out a clean 45-day gap from Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana — the year's other mega-event, which lands in November. Two tentpoles, two distinct audiences, no cannibalisation. This is the kind of strategic positioning that only happens when a studio knows exactly what it has.

And what they have looks extraordinary.

The Setup

King is reportedly inspired by Luc Besson's *Léon: The Professional* — the 1994 French thriller that turned Natalie Portman into a star. In this version, SRK plays a sleek, lethally precise assassin. Suhana Khan — making her theatrical debut — plays his young protégé drawn into his world. If the comparison holds, this is the kind of role that doesn't just launch a career; it announces one at full volume.

But it's the villain that might steal the conversation. Abhishek Bachchan has been cast as the primary antagonist, and if the reports are right, this is the darkest, most menacing role he's taken since *Dhoom* made him the coolest bad guy in Bollywood. Add Abhay Verma in a pivotal supporting role, and you've got a cast that's built for intensity.

> The industry buzz doesn't stop at the confirmed names. Deepika Padukone is rumoured for a powerful cameo, while Jaideep Ahlawat and Arshad Warsi are heavily linked to the project.

That ensemble alone makes this one of the most star-studded Hindi films in recent memory.

The Minds Behind It

Siddharth Anand directs — the man who gave us Pathaan, SRK's billion-rupee comeback after four years in the wilderness. That film didn't just work; it rewrote the rules for what a Hindi action film could earn. Pairing Anand with Khan again is the kind of move that tells you everyone involved is swinging for records.

The screenplay has serious firepower too. Sujoy Ghosh — the director of *Kahaani*, originally attached to helm King — co-wrote the story alongside Anand, Suresh Nair, and Sagar Pandya. Ghosh's thriller instincts with Anand's spectacle sense is a combination that reads like it was designed in a lab.

Production comes from Red Chillies Entertainment and Marflix Pictures, with a reported budget of ₹350 crore. For context, that's Pathaan-level money. This isn't a film — it's an event.

The Sound

Perhaps the most exciting detail for fans: Anirudh Ravichander is composing the soundtrack and background score. This marks his second collaboration with SRK after the record-smashing Jawan, whose music became almost as iconic as the film itself. Anirudh's ability to blend South Indian musical energy with mainstream Hindi hooks made Jawan's songs unavoidable — *Zinda Banda* alone lived on every playlist for months. Expect King to aim even higher.

The Diaspora Angle

For NRIs, the Christmas window is perfect. December 25 is a day off in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia — which means this opens on a day when the diaspora can actually show up in numbers. SRK's overseas pull hasn't dimmed; Pathaan collected over ₹300 crore internationally, and Jawan wasn't far behind. With King positioned as a global action spectacle, expect IMAX and premium format bookings to go fast.

Principal photography is reportedly nearing its final stages, with post-production planned on a global scale. The official announcement from the makers is expected within the coming week.

Mark the date. Christmas 2026 belongs to the King.
